**File: srs.md**

# 1. Introduction
### 1.1 Purpose
The purpose of this Software Requirements Specification (SRS) is to define the functional and non‑functional requirements for an Order Management System (OMS) that supports customers, order staff, and accountants.

### 1.2 Scope
The OMS enables customers to browse products, place orders, and make payments; order staff to receive, validate, fill, ship, and close orders; and accountants to issue invoices and process payments. The system stores all necessary data, enforces business rules, and records audit information.

### 1.3 Definitions and acronyms
- **Customer** – end‑user who purchases products.  
- **OrderStaff** – internal employee who processes orders.  
- **Accountant** – internal employee who handles invoicing and payments.  
- **DTO** – Data Transfer Object.  
- **TLS** – Transport Layer Security.

# 2. Overall description
### 2.1 Product perspective
The OMS is a stand‑alone web‑based application that persists data in a relational database and exposes a RESTful API to client applications.

### 2.2 Product functions
- Manage customer records (including optional bank account).  
- Manage product catalogue.  
- Create, validate and track orders and order items.  
- Issue invoices and record payments.  
- Enforce status transitions and business rules.  
- Audit all status changes.

### 2.3 User characteristics
- **Customer** – basic internet user, can view products and place orders.  
- **OrderStaff** – trained staff, authorized to change order statuses.  
- **Accountant** – trained staff, authorized to issue invoices and confirm/reject payments.

### 2.4 Assumptions and dependencies
- The system runs on a server with a SQL database.  
- All users are authenticated via an external identity provider.  
- TLS 1.2+ is available for encrypted communications.

# 3. Requirements
## 3.1 Functional requirements

| ID | User story |
|----|------------|
| **US-01** | As a **Customer**, I want to register my personal details (name, address, phone), so that the system can identify and contact me. |
| **US-02** | As a **Customer**, I want to add a single bank account to my profile (optional), so that I can use it as a payment method. |
| **US-03** | As a **Customer**, I want to view product information (name, description, price, image), so that I can decide what to buy. |
| **US-04** | As a **Customer**, I want to submit an order that contains at least one order item referencing existing products and a payment method, so that I can purchase the items. |
| **US-05** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to receive a submitted order and set its status to *pending*, so that the order enters the processing pipeline. |
| **US-06** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to mark a *pending* order as *filled*, so that the items are ready for shipping. |
| **US-07** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to decline a *pending* order, so that it is closed without fulfillment. |
| **US-08** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to ship a *filled* order, so that the customer receives the goods. |
| **US-09** | As an **Accountant**, I want to raise an invoice for a *filled* or *shipped* order that has no invoice, so that the order can be billed. |
| **US-10** | As an **Accountant**, I want to submit a payment against an *issued* invoice, so that the customer can settle the bill. |
| **US-11** | As an **Accountant**, I want to confirm a *pending* payment, so that the invoice becomes *paid*. |
| **US-12** | As an **Accountant**, I want to reject a *pending* payment, so that the failed payment is recorded and no further action is taken. |
| **US-13** | As an **Accountant**, I want to close a *shipped* order whose invoice is *paid*, so that the order lifecycle ends. |

### Acceptance criteria

#### US-01 – Customer registration
- **US-01-AC01** (condition) – The system requires **name**, **address**, and **phone**; any missing mandatory attribute causes the registration request to be rejected.  
- **US-01-AC02** (condition) – All three attributes are stored as non‑null strings.  
- **US-01-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a new registration request with all mandatory fields, When the request is processed, Then a Customer record is created and a unique Customer ID is returned.

#### US-02 – Optional bank account
- **US-02-AC01** (condition) – A Customer may have **zero or one** BankAccount; attempting to add a second bank account is rejected.  
- **US-02-AC02** (condition) – BankAccount stores **accountNumber** as a non‑empty string.  
- **US-02-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a Customer without a bank account, When the Customer adds a bank account, Then the BankAccount is stored and linked to the Customer.

#### US-03 – Product catalogue
- **US-03-AC01** (condition) – Every Product must have **name**, **description**, **price**, and **image**; missing any attribute causes the creation request to be rejected.  
- **US-03-AC02** (condition) – **price** is stored as a decimal number with two fractional digits.  
- **US-03-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a valid product definition, When the product is saved, Then it is persisted and can be referenced by OrderItems.

#### US-04 – Order submission
- **US-04-AC01** (condition) – An Order must reference **exactly one** existing Customer, contain **≥ 1** OrderItem, and store a **paymentMethod** (bank, card, cash).  
- **US-04-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given a known Customer and at least one OrderItem whose referenced Product exists, When the Customer submits the order, Then the system creates an Order with status *submitted*, sets **orderDate** to the submission date, and computes **totalAmount** as Σ(quantity × unitPrice).  
- **US-04-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given an unknown Customer, When the Customer attempts to submit an order, Then the request is rejected and no Order is created.  
- **US-04-AC04** (given_when_then) – Given an order with zero OrderItems, When the Customer submits it, Then the request is rejected and no Order is created.  
- **US-04-AC05** (given_when_then) – Given an OrderItem that references a non‑existent Product, When the order is submitted, Then the request is rejected and no Order is created.  
- **US-04-AC06** (condition) – OrderItem is **composed** within its Order; deleting an Order removes all its OrderItems.  
- **US-04-AC07** (condition) – OrderItem cannot be moved to another Order.

#### US-05 – Receive order
- **US-05-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given an Order with status *submitted*, When OrderStaff receives the order, Then the Order status becomes *pending*.  
- **US-05-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order whose status is not *submitted*, When OrderStaff attempts to receive it, Then the request is rejected and the status remains unchanged.  
- **US-05-AC03** (condition) – Allowed status transition: *submitted* → *pending* only.

#### US-06 – Fill order
- **US-06-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a *pending* Order, When OrderStaff marks it as *filled*, Then the Order status becomes *filled*.  
- **US-06-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order not in *pending* status, When OrderStaff attempts to fill it, Then the request is rejected and the status stays unchanged.  
- **US-06-AC03** (condition) – Allowed status transition: *pending* → *filled* or *pending* → *closed* (decline).

#### US-07 – Decline order
- **US-07-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a *pending* Order, When OrderStaff declines it, Then the Order status becomes *closed*.  
- **US-07-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order not in *pending* status, When OrderStaff attempts to decline it, Then the request is rejected and the status stays unchanged.  

#### US-08 – Ship order
- **US-08-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a *filled* Order, When OrderStaff ships it, Then the Order status becomes *shipped*.  
- **US-08-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order not in *filled* status, When OrderStaff attempts to ship it, Then the request is rejected and the status stays unchanged.  
- **US-08-AC03** (condition) – Shipping does **not** modify the status of any associated Invoice or Payment.

#### US-09 – Raise invoice
- **US-09-AC01** (condition) – An Invoice may be created only for an Order whose status is *filled* or *shipped* and that has **no existing** Invoice.  
- **US-09-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given such an Order, When Accountant raises an invoice, Then an Invoice is created with status *issued*, the supplied date, amount, and paymentMethod, and linked to the Order.  
- **US-09-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given an Order already having an Invoice, When Accountant attempts to raise another, Then the request is rejected.  
- **US-09-AC04** (given_when_then) – Given an Order with status *declined*, When Accountant attempts to raise an invoice, Then the request is rejected.

#### US-10 – Submit payment
- **US-10-AC01** (condition) – A Payment can be submitted only against an Invoice with status *issued*.  
- **US-10-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given such an Invoice, When Accountant records a payment, Then a Payment is created with status *pending* and the supplied date, amount, and paymentMethod.  
- **US-10-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given an Invoice whose status is *paid*, When a new payment is submitted, Then the request is rejected.

#### US-11 – Confirm payment
- **US-11-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment with status *pending* and its Invoice status *issued*, When Accountant confirms the payment, Then the Payment status becomes *completed* and the Invoice status becomes *paid*.  
- **US-11-AC02** (condition) – The Order status remains unchanged when its Invoice becomes *paid*.  
- **US-11-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment whose status is not *pending*, When Accountant attempts to confirm it, Then the request is rejected and the status remains unchanged.

#### US-12 – Reject payment
- **US-12-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment with status *pending*, When Accountant rejects it, Then the Payment status becomes *failed*; the Invoice and Order statuses stay unchanged.  
- **US-12-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment not in *pending* status, When Accountant attempts to reject it, Then the request is rejected.

#### US-13 – Close order
- **US-13-AC01** (condition) – An Order can be closed only when its status is *shipped* **and** its associated Invoice status is *paid*.  
- **US-13-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given such an Order, When Accountant closes it, Then the Order status becomes *closed*.  
- **US-13-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a *shipped* Order whose Invoice is not *paid*, When Accountant attempts to close it, Then the request is rejected and the Order status stays *shipped*.  
- **US-13-AC04** (given_when_then) – Given an Order with status *closed*, any further status‑change attempts are ignored and the status remains *closed*.

#### Cross‑cutting functional constraints (applied to all applicable stories)
- **Condition** – All monetary values (price, unit price, total amount, invoice amount, payment amount) are stored as decimal numbers. (REQ‑F‑46)  
- **Condition** – OrderStatus is limited to *submitted*, *pending*, *filled*, *shipped*, *closed* (REQ‑F‑47).  
- **Condition** – InvoiceStatus is limited to *issued*, *paid* (REQ‑F‑47).  
- **Condition** – PaymentStatus is limited to *pending*, *completed*, *failed* (REQ‑F‑47).  
- **Condition** – PaymentMethod on Order, Invoice, and Payment is limited to *bank*, *card*, *cash* (REQ‑F‑48).  
- **Condition** – Status changes must follow the allowed transition tables (REQ‑F‑49, REQ‑F‑50).  

## 3.2 Quality attributes
### 3.2.1 Performance
- **NFR-01** – When a user submits an order containing up to 50 order items under normal operating conditions, the system shall register the order and respond within **2 seconds** for at least **95 %** of submissions. (REQ‑N‑01)  
- **NFR-02** – Under normal operating conditions, the system shall support at least **200 concurrent users** and at least **20 order submissions per second** while meeting the response time of NFR‑01. (REQ‑N‑02)

### 3.2.2 Security
- **NFR-03** – The system shall authenticate every user before granting access to any customer, order, invoice or payment data, and shall reject **100 %** of unauthenticated requests. (REQ‑N‑05)  
- **NFR-04** – The system shall allow only users holding the **accountant** role to confirm or reject a payment, and shall reject the same request from any other user. (REQ‑N‑06)  
- **NFR-05** – The system shall protect customer personal data and bank account numbers by encrypting them in transit with **TLS 1.2 or higher** and at rest. (REQ‑N‑07)

### 3.2.3 Availability
- **NFR-06** – The system shall be available for at least **99.5 %** of each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance announced at least **24 hours** in advance. (REQ‑N‑03)  
- **NFR-07** – When a server failure occurs, the system shall resume accepting requests within **15 minutes** without losing any order, invoice or payment recorded before the failure. (REQ‑N‑04)

# 4. Verification
Verification of each functional requirement will be performed by automated acceptance‑test suites that execute the Given‑When‑Then scenarios. Non‑functional requirements will be verified by performance‑testing tools, security audits, and availability monitoring dashboards.

# 5. Supporting information
- PlantUML structural model: **structural.puml**  
- PlantUML behavioral model: **behavioral.puml**  
- Machine‑readable requirements list: **requirements.json**  
- Traceability matrix: **VMX.csv**

else (no)
  stop
endif
if (Order status == filled) then (yes)
  :ShipOrder;
  :Set status [shipped];
else (no)
  stop
endif
|Accountant|
if (Invoice exists && Invoice status == issued) then (yes)
  :SubmitPayment;
  :Create Payment [pending];
else (no)
  stop
endif
if (Payment status == pending) then (yes)
  if (Confirm?) then (yes)
    :ConfirmPayment;
    :Set Payment status [completed];
    :Set Invoice status [paid];
  else (no)
    :RejectPayment;
    :Set Payment status [failed];

  stop

**File: srs.md**

# 1. Introduction
### 1.1 Purpose
The purpose of this Software Requirements Specification (SRS) is to define the functional and non‑functional requirements for an Order Management System (OMS) that supports customers, order staff, and accountants.

### 1.2 Scope
The OMS enables customers to browse products, place orders, and make payments; order staff to receive, validate, fill, ship, and close orders; and accountants to issue invoices and process payments. The system stores all necessary data, enforces business rules, and records audit information.

### 1.3 Definitions and acronyms
- **Customer** – end‑user who purchases products.  
- **OrderStaff** – internal employee who processes orders.  
- **Accountant** – internal employee who handles invoicing and payments.  
- **DTO** – Data Transfer Object.  
- **TLS** – Transport Layer Security.

# 2. Overall description
### 2.1 Product perspective
The OMS is a stand‑alone web‑based application that persists data in a relational database and exposes a RESTful API to client applications.

### 2.2 Product functions
- Manage customer records (including optional bank account).  
- Manage product catalogue.  
- Create, validate and track orders and order items.  
- Issue invoices and record payments.  
- Enforce status transitions and business rules.  
- Audit all status changes.

### 2.3 User characteristics
- **Customer** – basic internet user, can view products and place orders.  
- **OrderStaff** – trained staff, authorized to change order statuses.  
- **Accountant** – trained staff, authorized to issue invoices and confirm/reject payments.

### 2.4 Assumptions and dependencies
- The system runs on a server with a SQL database.  
- All users are authenticated via an external identity provider.  
- TLS 1.2+ is available for encrypted communications.

# 3. Requirements
## 3.1 Functional requirements

| ID | User story |
|----|------------|
| **US-01** | As a **Customer**, I want to register my personal details (name, address, phone), so that the system can identify and contact me. |
| **US-02** | As a **Customer**, I want to add a single bank account to my profile (optional), so that I can use it as a payment method. |
| **US-03** | As a **Customer**, I want to view product information (name, description, price, image), so that I can decide what to buy. |
| **US-04** | As a **Customer**, I want to submit an order that contains at least one order item referencing existing products and a payment method, so that I can purchase the items. |
| **US-05** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to receive a submitted order and set its status to *pending*, so that the order enters the processing pipeline. |
| **US-06** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to mark a *pending* order as *filled*, so that the items are ready for shipping. |
| **US-07** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to decline a *pending* order, so that it is closed without fulfillment. |
| **US-08** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to ship a *filled* order, so that the customer receives the goods. |
| **US-09** | As an **Accountant**, I want to raise an invoice for a *filled* or *shipped* order that has no invoice, so that the order can be billed. |
| **US-10** | As an **Accountant**, I want to submit a payment against an *issued* invoice, so that the customer can settle the bill. |
| **US-11** | As an **Accountant**, I want to confirm a *pending* payment, so that the invoice becomes *paid*. |
| **US-12** | As an **Accountant**, I want to reject a *pending* payment, so that the failed payment is recorded and no further action is taken. |
| **US-13** | As an **Accountant**, I want to close a *shipped* order whose invoice is *paid*, so that the order lifecycle ends. |

### Acceptance criteria

#### US-01 – Customer registration
- **US-01-AC01** (condition) – The system requires **name**, **address**, and **phone**; any missing mandatory attribute causes the registration request to be rejected.  
- **US-01-AC02** (condition) – All three attributes are stored as non‑null strings.  
- **US-01-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a new registration request with all mandatory fields, When the request is processed, Then a Customer record is created and a unique Customer ID is returned.

#### US-02 – Optional bank account
- **US-02-AC01** (condition) – A Customer may have **zero or one** BankAccount; attempting to add a second bank account is rejected.  
- **US-02-AC02** (condition) – BankAccount stores **accountNumber** as a non‑empty string.  
- **US-02-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a Customer without a bank account, When the Customer adds a bank account, Then the BankAccount is stored and linked to the Customer.

#### US-03 – Product catalogue
- **US-03-AC01** (condition) – Every Product must have **name**, **description**, **price**, and **image**; missing any attribute causes the creation request to be rejected.  
- **US-03-AC02** (condition) – **price** is stored as a decimal number with two fractional digits.  
- **US-03-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a valid product definition, When the product is saved, Then it is persisted and can be referenced by OrderItems.

#### US-04 – Order submission
- **US-04-AC01** (condition) – An Order must reference **exactly one** existing Customer, contain **≥ 1** OrderItem, and store a **paymentMethod** (bank, card, cash).  
- **US-04-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given a known Customer and at least one OrderItem whose referenced Product exists, When the Customer submits the order, Then the system creates an Order with status *submitted*, sets **orderDate** to the submission date, and computes **totalAmount** as Σ(quantity × unitPrice).  
- **US-04-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given an unknown Customer, When the Customer attempts to submit an order, Then the request is rejected and no Order is created.  
- **US-04-AC04** (given_when_then) – Given an order with zero OrderItems, When the Customer submits it, Then the request is rejected and no Order is created.  
- **US-04-AC05** (given_when_then) – Given an OrderItem that references a non‑existent Product, When the order is submitted, Then the request is rejected and no Order is created.  
- **US-04-AC06** (condition) – OrderItem is **composed** within its Order; deleting an Order removes all its OrderItems.  
- **US-04-AC07** (condition) – OrderItem cannot be moved to another Order.

#### US-05 – Receive order
- **US-05-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given an Order with status *submitted*, When OrderStaff receives the order, Then the Order status becomes *pending*.  
- **US-05-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order whose status is not *submitted*, When OrderStaff attempts to receive it, Then the request is rejected and the status remains unchanged.  
- **US-05-AC03** (condition) – Allowed status transition: *submitted* → *pending* only.

#### US-06 – Fill order
- **US-06-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a *pending* Order, When OrderStaff marks it as *filled*, Then the Order status becomes *filled*.  
- **US-06-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order not in *pending* status, When OrderStaff attempts to fill it, Then the request is rejected and the status stays unchanged.  
- **US-06-AC03** (condition) – Allowed status transition: *pending* → *filled* or *pending* → *closed* (decline).

#### US-07 – Decline order
- **US-07-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a *pending* Order, When OrderStaff declines it, Then the Order status becomes *closed*.  
- **US-07-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order not in *pending* status, When OrderStaff attempts to decline it, Then the request is rejected and the status stays unchanged.  

#### US-08 – Ship order
- **US-08-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a *filled* Order, When OrderStaff ships it, Then the Order status becomes *shipped*.  
- **US-08-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order not in *filled* status, When OrderStaff attempts to ship it, Then the request is rejected and the status stays unchanged.  
- **US-08-AC03** (condition) – Shipping does **not** modify the status of any associated Invoice or Payment.

#### US-09 – Raise invoice
- **US-09-AC01** (condition) – An Invoice may be created only for an Order whose status is *filled* or *shipped* and that has **no existing** Invoice.  
- **US-09-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given such an Order, When Accountant raises an invoice, Then an Invoice is created with status *issued*, the supplied date, amount, and paymentMethod, and linked to the Order.  
- **US-09-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given an Order already having an Invoice, When Accountant attempts to raise another, Then the request is rejected.  
- **US-09-AC04** (given_when_then) – Given an Order with status *declined*, When Accountant attempts to raise an invoice, Then the request is rejected.

#### US-10 – Submit payment
- **US-10-AC01** (condition) – A Payment can be submitted only against an Invoice with status *issued*.  
- **US-10-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given such an Invoice, When Accountant records a payment, Then a Payment is created with status *pending* and the supplied date, amount, and paymentMethod.  
- **US-10-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given an Invoice whose status is *paid*, When a new payment is submitted, Then the request is rejected.

#### US-11 – Confirm payment
- **US-11-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment with status *pending* and its Invoice status *issued*, When Accountant confirms the payment, Then the Payment status becomes *completed* and the Invoice status becomes *paid*.  
- **US-11-AC02** (condition) – The Order status remains unchanged when its Invoice becomes *paid*.  
- **US-11-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment whose status is not *pending*, When Accountant attempts to confirm it, Then the request is rejected and the status remains unchanged.

#### US-12 – Reject payment
- **US-12-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment with status *pending*, When Accountant rejects it, Then the Payment status becomes *failed*; the Invoice and Order statuses stay unchanged.  
- **US-12-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment not in *pending* status, When Accountant attempts to reject it, Then the request is rejected.

#### US-13 – Close order
- **US-13-AC01** (condition) – An Order can be closed only when its status is *shipped* **and** its associated Invoice status is *paid*.  
- **US-13-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given such an Order, When Accountant closes it, Then the Order status becomes *closed*.  
- **US-13-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a *shipped* Order whose Invoice is not *paid*, When Accountant attempts to close it, Then the request is rejected and the Order status stays *shipped*.  
- **US-13-AC04** (given_when_then) – Given an Order with status *closed*, any further status‑change attempts are ignored and the status remains *closed*.

#### Cross‑cutting functional constraints (applied to all applicable stories)
- **Condition** – All monetary values (price, unit price, total amount, invoice amount, payment amount) are stored as decimal numbers. (REQ‑F‑46)  
- **Condition** – OrderStatus is limited to *submitted*, *pending*, *filled*, *shipped*, *closed* (REQ‑F‑47).  
- **Condition** – InvoiceStatus is limited to *issued*, *paid* (REQ‑F‑47).  
- **Condition** – PaymentStatus is limited to *pending*, *completed*, *failed* (REQ‑F‑47).  
- **Condition** – PaymentMethod on Order, Invoice, and Payment is limited to *bank*, *card*, *cash* (REQ‑F‑48).  
- **Condition** – Status changes must follow the allowed transition tables (REQ‑F‑49, REQ‑F‑50).  

## 3.2 Quality attributes
### 3.2.1 Performance
- **NFR-01** – When a user submits an order containing up to 50 order items under normal operating conditions, the system shall register the order and respond within **2 seconds** for at least **95 %** of submissions. (REQ‑N‑01)  
- **NFR-02** – Under normal operating conditions, the system shall support at least **200 concurrent users** and at least **20 order submissions per second** while meeting the response time of NFR‑01. (REQ‑N‑02)

### 3.2.2 Security
- **NFR-03** – The system shall authenticate every user before granting access to any customer, order, invoice or payment data, and shall reject **100 %** of unauthenticated requests. (REQ‑N‑05)  
- **NFR-04** – The system shall allow only users holding the **accountant** role to confirm or reject a payment, and shall reject the same request from any other user. (REQ‑N‑06)  
- **NFR-05** – The system shall protect customer personal data and bank account numbers by encrypting them in transit with **TLS 1.2 or higher** and at rest. (REQ‑N‑07)

### 3.2.3 Availability
- **NFR-06** – The system shall be available for at least **99.5 %** of each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance announced at least **24 hours** in advance. (REQ‑N‑03)  
- **NFR-07** – When a server failure occurs, the system shall resume accepting requests within **15 minutes** without losing any order, invoice or payment recorded before the failure. (REQ‑N‑04)

# 4. Verification
Verification of each functional requirement will be performed by automated acceptance‑test suites that execute the Given‑When‑Then scenarios. Non‑functional requirements will be verified by performance‑testing tools, security audits, and availability monitoring dashboards.

# 5. Supporting information
- PlantUML structural model: **structural.puml**  
- PlantUML behavioral model: **behavioral.puml**  
- Machine‑readable requirements list: **requirements.json**  
- Traceability matrix: **VMX.csv**  



**File: structural.puml**

@startuml structural
' Enumerations
enum OrderStatus {
  submitted
  pending
  filled
  shipped
  closed
}
enum InvoiceStatus {
  issued
  paid
}
enum PaymentStatus {
  pending
  completed
  failed
}
enum PaymentMethod {
  bank
  card
  cash
}

' Domain classes
class Customer {
  +String name
  +String address
  +String phone
}
class BankAccount {
  +String accountNumber
}
class Product {
  +String name
  +String description
  +Decimal price
  +String imageUrl
}
class Order {
  +Date orderDate
  +Decimal totalAmount
  +OrderStatus status
  +PaymentMethod paymentMethod
}
class OrderItem {
  +Integer quantity
  +Decimal unitPrice
}
class Invoice {
  +Date date
  +Decimal amount
  +InvoiceStatus status
  +PaymentMethod paymentMethod
}
class Payment {
  +Date date
  +Decimal amount
  +PaymentStatus status
  +PaymentMethod paymentMethod
}

' Relationships
Customer "1" o-- "0..1" BankAccount : has
Customer "1" <-- "0..*" Order : places
Order "1" o-- "0..1" Invoice : generates
Invoice "1" o-- "1..*" Payment : records
Order "1" o-- "1..*" OrderItem : contains
OrderItem "1" --> "1" Product : references
@enduml



**File: behavioral.puml**

@startuml behavioral
' Swimlanes
|Customer|
start
:SubmitOrder;
if (Order valid?) then (yes)
  :Create Order [submitted];
else (no)
  stop
endif
|OrderStaff|
if (Order status == submitted) then (yes)
  :ReceiveOrder;
  :Set status [pending];
else (no)
  stop
endif
if (Order status == pending) then (yes)
  split
    :MarkOrderFilled;
    :Set status [filled];
  split again
    :RaiseInvoice;
    :Create Invoice [issued];
  end split
else (no)
  stop
endif
if (Order status == filled) then (yes)
  :ShipOrder;
  :Set status [shipped];
else (no)
  stop
endif
|Accountant|
if (Invoice exists && Invoice status == issued) then (yes)
  :SubmitPayment;
  :Create Payment [pending];
else (no)
  stop
endif
if (Payment status == pending) then (yes)
  if (Confirm?) then (yes)
    :ConfirmPayment;
    :Set Payment status [completed];
    :Set Invoice status [paid];
  else (no)
    :RejectPayment;
    :Set Payment status [failed];
  endif
else (no)
  stop
endif
if (Order status == shipped && Invoice status == paid) then (yes)
  :CloseOrder;
  :Set Order status [closed];
else (no)
  stop
endif
stop
@enduml

**File: srs.md**

# 1. Introduction
### 1.1 Purpose
The purpose of this Software Requirements Specification (SRS) is to define the functional and non‑functional requirements for an Order Management System (OMS) that supports customers, order staff, and accountants.

### 1.2 Scope
The OMS enables customers to browse products, place orders, and make payments; order staff to receive, validate, fill, ship, and close orders; and accountants to issue invoices and process payments. The system stores all necessary data, enforces business rules, and records audit information.

### 1.3 Definitions and acronyms
- **Customer** – end‑user who purchases products.  
- **OrderStaff** – internal employee who processes orders.  
- **Accountant** – internal employee who handles invoicing and payments.  
- **DTO** – Data Transfer Object.  
- **TLS** – Transport Layer Security.

# 2. Overall description
### 2.1 Product perspective
The OMS is a stand‑alone web‑based application that persists data in a relational database and exposes a RESTful API to client applications.

### 2.2 Product functions
- Manage customer records (including optional bank account).  
- Manage product catalogue.  
- Create, validate and track orders and order items.  
- Issue invoices and record payments.  
- Enforce status transitions and business rules.  
- Audit all status changes.

### 2.3 User characteristics
- **Customer** – basic internet user, can view products and place orders.  
- **OrderStaff** – trained staff, authorized to change order statuses.  
- **Accountant** – trained staff, authorized to issue invoices and confirm/reject payments.

### 2.4 Assumptions and dependencies
- The system runs on a server with a SQL database.  
- All users are authenticated via an external identity provider.  
- TLS 1.2+ is available for encrypted communications.

# 3. Requirements
## 3.1 Functional requirements

| ID | User story |
|----|------------|
| **US-01** | As a **Customer**, I want to register my personal details (name, address, phone), so that the system can identify and contact me. |
| **US-02** | As a **Customer**, I want to add a single bank account to my profile (optional), so that I can use it as a payment method. |
| **US-03** | As a **Customer**, I want to view product information (name, description, price, image), so that I can decide what to buy. |
| **US-04** | As a **Customer**, I want to submit an order that contains at least one order item referencing existing products and a payment method, so that I can purchase the items. |
| **US-05** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to receive a submitted order and set its status to *pending*, so that the order enters the processing pipeline. |
| **US-06** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to mark a *pending* order as *filled*, so that the items are ready for shipping. |
| **US-07** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to decline a *pending* order, so that it is closed without fulfillment. |
| **US-08** | As an **OrderStaff**, I want to ship a *filled* order, so that the customer receives the goods. |
| **US-09** | As an **Accountant**, I want to raise an invoice for a *filled* or *shipped* order that has no invoice, so that the order can be billed. |
| **US-10** | As an **Accountant**, I want to submit a payment against an *issued* invoice, so that the customer can settle the bill. |
| **US-11** | As an **Accountant**, I want to confirm a *pending* payment, so that the invoice becomes *paid*. |
| **US-12** | As an **Accountant**, I want to reject a *pending* payment, so that the failed payment is recorded and no further action is taken. |
| **US-13** | As an **Accountant**, I want to close a *shipped* order whose invoice is *paid*, so that the order lifecycle ends. |

### Acceptance criteria

#### US-01 – Customer registration
- **US-01-AC01** (condition) – The system requires **name**, **address**, and **phone**; any missing mandatory attribute causes the registration request to be rejected.  
- **US-01-AC02** (condition) – All three attributes are stored as non‑null strings.  
- **US-01-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a new registration request with all mandatory fields, When the request is processed, Then a Customer record is created and a unique Customer ID is returned.

#### US-02 – Optional bank account
- **US-02-AC01** (condition) – A Customer may have **zero or one** BankAccount; attempting to add a second bank account is rejected.  
- **US-02-AC02** (condition) – BankAccount stores **accountNumber** as a non‑empty string.  
- **US-02-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a Customer without a bank account, When the Customer adds a bank account, Then the BankAccount is stored and linked to the Customer.

#### US-03 – Product catalogue
- **US-03-AC01** (condition) – Every Product must have **name**, **description**, **price**, and **image**; missing any attribute causes the creation request to be rejected.  
- **US-03-AC02** (condition) – **price** is stored as a decimal number with two fractional digits.  
- **US-03-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a valid product definition, When the product is saved, Then it is persisted and can be referenced by OrderItems.

#### US-04 – Order submission
- **US-04-AC01** (condition) – An Order must reference **exactly one** existing Customer, contain **≥ 1** OrderItem, and store a **paymentMethod** (bank, card, cash).  
- **US-04-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given a known Customer and at least one OrderItem whose referenced Product exists, When the Customer submits the order, Then the system creates an Order with status *submitted*, sets **orderDate** to the submission date, and computes **totalAmount** as Σ(quantity × unitPrice).  
- **US-04-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given an unknown Customer, When the Customer attempts to submit an order, Then the request is rejected and no Order is created.  
- **US-04-AC04** (given_when_then) – Given an order with zero OrderItems, When the Customer submits it, Then the request is rejected and no Order is created.  
- **US-04-AC05** (given_when_then) – Given an OrderItem that references a non‑existent Product, When the order is submitted, Then the request is rejected and no Order is created.  
- **US-04-AC06** (condition) – OrderItem is **composed** within its Order; deleting an Order removes all its OrderItems.  
- **US-04-AC07** (condition) – OrderItem cannot be moved to another Order.

#### US-05 – Receive order
- **US-05-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given an Order with status *submitted*, When OrderStaff receives the order, Then the Order status becomes *pending*.  
- **US-05-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order whose status is not *submitted*, When OrderStaff attempts to receive it, Then the request is rejected and the status remains unchanged.  
- **US-05-AC03** (condition) – Allowed status transition: *submitted* → *pending* only.

#### US-06 – Fill order
- **US-06-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a *pending* Order, When OrderStaff marks it as *filled*, Then the Order status becomes *filled*.  
- **US-06-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order not in *pending* status, When OrderStaff attempts to fill it, Then the request is rejected and the status stays unchanged.  
- **US-06-AC03** (condition) – Allowed status transition: *pending* → *filled* or *pending* → *closed* (decline).

#### US-07 – Decline order
- **US-07-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a *pending* Order, When OrderStaff declines it, Then the Order status becomes *closed*.  
- **US-07-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order not in *pending* status, When OrderStaff attempts to decline it, Then the request is rejected and the status stays unchanged.  

#### US-08 – Ship order
- **US-08-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a *filled* Order, When OrderStaff ships it, Then the Order status becomes *shipped*.  
- **US-08-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given an Order not in *filled* status, When OrderStaff attempts to ship it, Then the request is rejected and the status stays unchanged.  
- **US-08-AC03** (condition) – Shipping does **not** modify the status of any associated Invoice or Payment.

#### US-09 – Raise invoice
- **US-09-AC01** (condition) – An Invoice may be created only for an Order whose status is *filled* or *shipped* and that has **no existing** Invoice.  
- **US-09-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given such an Order, When Accountant raises an invoice, Then an Invoice is created with status *issued*, the supplied date, amount, and paymentMethod, and linked to the Order.  
- **US-09-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given an Order already having an Invoice, When Accountant attempts to raise another, Then the request is rejected.  
- **US-09-AC04** (given_when_then) – Given an Order with status *declined*, When Accountant attempts to raise an invoice, Then the request is rejected.

#### US-10 – Submit payment
- **US-10-AC01** (condition) – A Payment can be submitted only against an Invoice with status *issued*.  
- **US-10-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given such an Invoice, When Accountant records a payment, Then a Payment is created with status *pending* and the supplied date, amount, and paymentMethod.  
- **US-10-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given an Invoice whose status is *paid*, When a new payment is submitted, Then the request is rejected.

#### US-11 – Confirm payment
- **US-11-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment with status *pending* and its Invoice status *issued*, When Accountant confirms the payment, Then the Payment status becomes *completed* and the Invoice status becomes *paid*.  
- **US-11-AC02** (condition) – The Order status remains unchanged when its Invoice becomes *paid*.  
- **US-11-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment whose status is not *pending*, When Accountant attempts to confirm it, Then the request is rejected and the status remains unchanged.

#### US-12 – Reject payment
- **US-12-AC01** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment with status *pending*, When Accountant rejects it, Then the Payment status becomes *failed*; the Invoice and Order statuses stay unchanged.  
- **US-12-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given a Payment not in *pending* status, When Accountant attempts to reject it, Then the request is rejected.

#### US-13 – Close order
- **US-13-AC01** (condition) – An Order can be closed only when its status is *shipped* **and** its associated Invoice status is *paid*.  
- **US-13-AC02** (given_when_then) – Given such an Order, When Accountant closes it, Then the Order status becomes *closed*.  
- **US-13-AC03** (given_when_then) – Given a *shipped* Order whose Invoice is not *paid*, When Accountant attempts to close it, Then the request is rejected and the Order status stays *shipped*.  
- **US-13-AC04** (given_when_then) – Given an Order with status *closed*, any further status‑change attempts are ignored and the status remains *closed*.

#### Cross‑cutting functional constraints (applied to all applicable stories)
- **Condition** – All monetary values (price, unit price, total amount, invoice amount, payment amount) are stored as decimal numbers. (REQ‑F‑46)  
- **Condition** – OrderStatus is limited to *submitted*, *pending*, *filled*, *shipped*, *closed* (REQ‑F‑47).  
- **Condition** – InvoiceStatus is limited to *issued*, *paid* (REQ‑F‑47).  
- **Condition** – PaymentStatus is limited to *pending*, *completed*, *failed* (REQ‑F‑47).  
- **Condition** – PaymentMethod on Order, Invoice, and Payment is limited to *bank*, *card*, *cash* (REQ‑F‑48).  
- **Condition** – Status changes must follow the allowed transition tables (REQ‑F‑49, REQ‑F‑50).  

## 3.2 Quality attributes
### 3.2.1 Performance
- **NFR-01** – When a user submits an order containing up to 50 order items under normal operating conditions, the system shall register the order and respond within **2 seconds** for at least **95 %** of submissions. (REQ‑N‑01)  
- **NFR-02** – Under normal operating conditions, the system shall support at least **200 concurrent users** and at least **20 order submissions per second** while meeting the response time of NFR‑01. (REQ‑N‑02)

### 3.2.2 Security
- **NFR-03** – The system shall authenticate every user before granting access to any customer, order, invoice or payment data, and shall reject **100 %** of unauthenticated requests. (REQ‑N‑05)  
- **NFR-04** – The system shall allow only users holding the **accountant** role to confirm or reject a payment, and shall reject the same request from any other user. (REQ‑N‑06)  
- **NFR-05** – The system shall protect customer personal data and bank account numbers by encrypting them in transit with **TLS 1.2 or higher** and at rest. (REQ‑N‑07)

### 3.2.3 Availability
- **NFR-06** – The system shall be available for at least **99.5 %** of each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance announced at least **24 hours** in advance. (REQ‑N‑03)  
- **NFR-07** – When a server failure occurs, the system shall resume accepting requests within **15 minutes** without losing any order, invoice or payment recorded before the failure. (REQ‑N‑04)

# 4. Verification
Verification of each functional requirement will be performed by automated acceptance‑test suites that execute the Given‑When‑Then scenarios. Non‑functional requirements will be verified by performance‑testing tools, security audits, and availability monitoring dashboards.

@startuml structural
' Enumerations
enum OrderStatus {
  submitted
  pending
  filled
  shipped
  closed
}
enum InvoiceStatus {
  issued
  paid
}
enum PaymentStatus {
  pending
  completed
  failed
}
enum PaymentMethod {
  bank
  card
  cash
}

' Domain classes
class Customer {
  +String name
  +String address
  +String phone
}
class BankAccount {
  +String accountNumber
}
class Product {
  +String name
  +String description
  +Decimal price
  +String imageUrl
}
class Order {
  +Date orderDate
  +Decimal totalAmount
  +OrderStatus status
  +PaymentMethod paymentMethod
}
class OrderItem {
  +Integer quantity
  +Decimal unitPrice
}
class Invoice {
  +Date date
  +Decimal amount
  +InvoiceStatus status
  +PaymentMethod paymentMethod
}
class Payment {
  +Date date
  +Decimal amount
  +PaymentStatus status
  +PaymentMethod paymentMethod
}

' Relationships
Customer "1" o-- "0..1" BankAccount : has
Customer "1" <-- "0..*" Order : places
Order "1" o-- "0..1" Invoice : generates
Invoice "1" o-- "1..*" Payment : records
Order "1" o-- "1..*" OrderItem : contains
OrderItem "1" --> "1" Product : references
@enduml



**File: behavioral.puml**

@startuml behavioral
' Swimlanes
|Customer|
start
:SubmitOrder;
if (Order valid?) then (yes)
  :Create Order [submitted];
else (no)
  stop
endif
|OrderStaff|
if (Order status == submitted) then (yes)
  :ReceiveOrder;
  :Set status [pending];
else (no)
  stop
endif
if (Order status == pending) then (yes)
  split
    :MarkOrderFilled;
    :Set status [filled];
  split again
    :RaiseInvoice;
    :Create Invoice [issued];
  end split
else (no)
  stop
endif
if (Order status == filled) then (yes)
  :ShipOrder;
  :Set status [shipped];
else (no)
  stop
endif
|Accountant|
if (Invoice exists && Invoice status == issued) then (yes)
  :SubmitPayment;
  :Create Payment [pending];
else (no)
  stop
endif
if (Payment status == pending) then (yes)
  if (Confirm?) then (yes)
    :ConfirmPayment;
    :Set Payment status [completed];
    :Set Invoice status [paid];
  else (no)
    :RejectPayment;
    :Set Payment status [failed];
  endif
else (no)
  stop
endif
if (Order status == shipped && Invoice status == paid) then (yes)
  :CloseOrder;
  :Set Order status [closed];
else (no)
  stop
endif
stop
@enduml
